Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The test `testAvailableLocaleSet` calls the static method `LocaleUtils.availableLocaleSet()` which returns a set of available locales. Inspecting the `availableLocaleSet()` method reveals that it uses a private static field `cAvailableLocaleSet` which is initially null. The method checks if `cAvailableLocaleSet` is null, and if so, initializes it with a new unmodifiable set built from the list `availableLocaleList()`. 

The field `cAvailableLocaleSet` is declared as:
```java
private static Set cAvailableLocaleSet;
```
and it is not initialized at declaration.

The test fails because FindBugs reports a warning: the field `cAvailableLocaleSet` is not initialized in the constructor (nor at declaration), and can be null if `availableLocaleSet()` has not been called yet. This leads to a `NullPointerException` when `cAvailableLocaleSet` is accessed directly elsewhere without checking if it is null.

Indeed, `isAvailableLocale(Locale)` directly calls `cAvailableLocaleSet.contains(locale)` without null checks:
```java
public static boolean isAvailableLocale(Locale locale) {
    return cAvailableLocaleSet.contains(locale);
}
```
If `cAvailableLocaleSet` was not initialized by calling `availableLocaleSet()`, it remains null, and invoking `contains()` on it results in a `NullPointerException`.

The root cause is that the static field `cAvailableLocaleSet` is lazy-initialized only when `availableLocaleSet()` is called. If other methods access this field without initialization, a `NullPointerException` occurs.

Therefore, the bug is due to an uninitialized static field `cAvailableLocaleSet` accessed without null checks resulting in NPE.

No recent bug reports seem relevant since they address unrelated issues.

Suggestion would be to ensure `cAvailableLocaleSet` is initialized eagerly or lazily but check for null before usage, or force initialization in the class static initializer. 

This explains the failure in the test and the issue raised by the bug report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
